(4) Velocity

Eastward, northward and upward velocity, current speed, and the direction toward which the current flows (relative to true north, declination applied), interpolated linearly in pressure between the 7 current meters (triangles at right); no values above the shallowest or below the deepest. One colour scale for the three components, symmetric about zero, to the larger magnitude of the 1st and 99th percentiles; speed (to its 98th percentile) and direction (a cyclic scale, 0–360°, clockwise from north) have their own. Buoyancy frequency squared (log₁₀ N², s⁻²), calculated simply between neighbouring 50 dbar levels of the gridded temperature and salinity (GSW, no adiabatic levelling). Because the grid is interpolated linearly in pressure between instruments, N² changes mostly at the instrument pressures; zero or negative values are drawn in the lowest colour. For analysis, calculate N² from the measurements yourself.

(7) Overflow

Isopycnal coverage diagnostic. Percentage of time steps during which each σ₀ surface (0.1 kg/m³ spacing) lies within the measured column range. Green ≥ 80 %; amber 50–80 %; red < 50 %. Orange diamond: the target σ₀. Dashed line: 80 %. Gaps in the tracking figure correspond to times when the isopycnal is outside the measured range (above the shallowest grid level, or below the deepest).

show / hide
source: oceanarray/plotters/hydrography.py:draw_isopycnal_coverage

Isopycnal height above seabed — sigma0. Height above seabed (m) of each target σ₀ surface through time. Tracked by linear interpolation in density space from the gridded sigma0 field; 1-hour running median applied. Blank where the surface outcrops or is outside the observed range. Light blue = lighter water (shallower); dark blue = denser water (deeper). Default target σ₀ = 27.70.

show / hide
source: oceanarray/plotters/hydrography.py:draw_isopycnal_ts

Temperature ~100 m above seabed. 1-hour running median temperature at the grid pressure level nearest to 100 m above the seabed. Level and height-above-seabed shown in figure title.

(8) Frequency analysis

Power spectral density of temperature at 5 levels (Welch estimate): 250, 350, 450, 650 and 750 dbar, the grid levels nearest the instruments with values at least 90 % of the time, shallowest, deepest and evenly between (colour bar). Left: 5.3-day Hann windows (shortened from 14 days: the record is 14 days long); right: 3.4-day Hann windows (shortened from 7 days: the record is 14 days long), zoomed to periods under 2 days; 50 % overlap. Vertical lines: M2 (12.4 h), K1 (23.9 h), inertial period (13.1 h at this latitude). Dashed: a −2 slope for reference. Also marked, from the mooring description: 1.8 d and 4 d. Not drawn (outside the periods shown): 9 min.

show / hide
source: oceanarray/plotters/spectrum.py:draw_spectrum

Wavelet power of temperature at 250, 500 and 750 dbar (Morlet, ω₀ = 6; Torrence & Compo 1998), log₁₀ °C² d: the outermost levels with values at least 90 % of the time and one between. Hatched: edge-affected (cone of influence); cross-hatched: gaps filled before the transform. Black contours: 95 % significance against red noise. Periods from 6 hours up.

show / hide
source: oceanarray/plotters/spectrum.py:draw_wavelet

Rotary spectra of velocity at 350 and 450 dbar: clockwise (red, solid) and counter-clockwise (blue, dashed) components, and the rotary coefficient r = (CCW − CW)/(CCW + CW) (right; r < 0: clockwise dominant). Welch estimate, 5.3-day Hann windows (shortened from 14 days: the record is 14 days long), 50 % overlap. Vertical lines: M2, K1 and the inertial period f. Clockwise rotation near f and the tides is expected for internal waves in the Northern Hemisphere. Also marked, from the mooring description: 1.8 d and 4 d. Not drawn (outside the periods shown): 9 min.
